card: This pull request updates Tapscript Miniscript duplicate-key validation to compare public keys as 32-byte x-only keys rather than full 33-byte compressed keys. Previously, tr() descriptors containing keys that differed only by parity passed sanity checks even though they serialize to identical scripts on-chain. This violated BIP-379 duplicate key guarantees and permitted third-party transaction malleability through branch flipping. P2WSH descriptor parsing remains unaffected and continues to distinguish 33-byte compressed keys.
changed_since_previous: The implementation now provides complete diffs and unit test additions verifying both tr() descriptor rejection and continued wsh() parsing of distinct 33-byte compressed keys.
evidence: Commit 0956ace45d and PR description cite BIP-379: 'BIP-379 malleability analysis relies on the invariant that no public key is repeated. Because one signature satisfies both branches, a third party can malleate transactions by flipping the branch selector without possessing the private key.'
Linked issue #36414 demonstrates that tr() descriptors previously marked scripts with identical x-coordinates and different parities as sane.
problem: When a tr() Miniscript descriptor contains keys that differ only in parity prefix (such as pk(02X) and pk(03X)), KeyParser::KeyCompare previously treated them as distinct 33-byte keys and passed sanity checks. Because Tapscript drops key parity on-chain, both branches serialize to identical scripts, violating BIP-379 invariants against duplicate keys and allowing third parties to malleate transactions by switching execution branches without possessing private keys.

risk.why: A mistake in descriptor key comparison could falsely reject valid descriptors or fail to detect duplicate keys, impacting descriptor-based wallet imports and script sanity checks.

summary: Compares public keys as 32-byte x-only public keys instead of 33-byte compressed keys during Miniscript duplicate-key checks in Tapscript descriptors. In a Tapscript context, keys sharing an x-coordinate but differing in parity byte are now detected as identical, causing DuplicateKeyCheck() to fail and mark the descriptor as not sane. Segwit v0 descriptors continue to distinguish full 33-byte keys.
